title: How Go1 and OpenAI are helping organizations build AI capability at scale
summary: Go1 is partnering with OpenAI to make OpenAI Academy courses available through its global learning ecosystem, helping HR and L&D teams build workforce AI capability.
body_markdown:
This can help organizations:


- Make practical AI training available to more employees
- Give different roles access to learning that matches their needs
- Connect AI education with existing workforce development programs
- Monitor learner participation and engagement
- Identify new learning priorities as AI adoption develops


AI capability is not built through a single course. It needs to develop as tools, workflows and expectations change.


## What does AI capability look like across an organization?


AI capability doesn't look the same for everyone. Our[Keeping Pace: Leading Learning in the Age of AI](https://www.go1.com/reports/ai-learning-research-report) report, based on responses from more than 2,000 employees and L&D professionals, found that AI adoption is uneven across roles. Technology and customer service teams are leading the way, while many employees still use AI infrequently.


That uneven adoption means a single learning program for all employees is unlikely to work. Different groups need different entry points, examples and opportunities to practice.


**For employees:** AI capability may start with writing clearer prompts, checking AI outputs and using AI to support routine work. Inside our[guide to AI training for employees,](https://www.go1.com/blog/ai-training) we’ve identified AI literacy, prompting, critical thinking and responsible use as core parts of workplace AI training.


**For leaders:** AI capability includes understanding where AI can create value, setting clear expectations and communicating a direction employees can follow.


The skills employees need are evolving as well. In Keeping Pace, our research highlights growing interest in data literacy, prompt engineering, AI ethics and human-AI collaboration. These capabilities help people evaluate AI outputs, make informed decisions and work effectively with AI as it becomes part of everyday processes.


OpenAI Academy’s range of learning can help organizations respond to these different needs. Employees, leaders, technical teams and educators can build capability that is relevant to their work, while the organization develops a common foundation for[AI adoption](https://www.go1.com/solutions/category/generative-ai) .


## How does the Go1 and OpenAI partnership support workforce readiness?


Workforce readiness depends on more than knowing that AI exists. People need to understand how it applies to their work and where human judgment remains essential. The Go1 and OpenAI partnership gives organizations a way to connect broad AI education with more specialized learning for different roles.


For HR and L&D leaders, this connects AI training with priorities such as productivity, innovation, employee development and[future skills](https://www.go1.com/blog/ai-training) . Learning data can then help teams monitor engagement and inform future learning priorities.


## What should organizations do next?


Organizations[preparing their workforce for AI](https://www.go1.com/blog/ai-training) should begin by identifying the roles, audiences and use cases that matter most. This helps HR and L&D teams decide where foundational AI literacy is needed and where employees require more specialized, role-based training.


From there, they can combine foundational AI learning with role-specific development and use[Go1 Reporting & Insights](https://www.go1.com/product/reporting-insights) to track engagement, progress, and assess emerging capability needs. Teams can use those insights to decide where further support is needed as employees gain experience.


OpenAI Academy courses will be available through Go1 from November 4th, 2026.


To learn more, visit the[Go1 and OpenAI partnership page](https://www.go1.com/openai-academy) .
